quote: But what if he did exist? What if Reddington was real? If he was, I could use his story and all that it provided to protect my daughter while watching over her from a distance.
context: Katarina explains her motivation for creating a real Reddington persona.

quote: If he wasn't dead, you'd never know you'd killed him. No one knew your father was dead. The KGB, the FBI, CIA... The entire alphabet was looking for the man that they thought had betrayed his country and abandoned his family. Which meant they were chasing a man who never existed.
context: Katarina explains the strategic value of Reddington's unknown death to Elizabeth.

quote: 13 packets of intelligence that could be used to blackmail and leverage anyone from the Russian Vory, to captains of industry, to heads of state. Greed and corruption trickle down and turn into crime on the way to the gutter.
context: Katarina explains how the Sikorsky Archive was used to build Reddington's power.

quote: This story is all about you, Masha. Protecting you. And then protecting your daughter.
context: Katarina summarizes the entire narrative as being centered on Elizabeth's protection.

quote: What emerged was an intelligence network that was built for one reason: To keep you safe.
context: Katarina reveals the ultimate purpose of the Blacklist network.

quote: The fighting, the gunshot, the death of your father... those flames... I was desperate to erase that night from your memory.
context: Katarina explains why she had Elizabeth's memory erased after the fire.

quote: I haven't slept through the night in 25 years. Tonight, I'll sleep like a baby.
context: Reddington offers Townsend everything he has in exchange for Elizabeth's life.

quote: I couldn't save your father. I couldn't lose you, too.
context: Katarina explains her desperate decision to give Elizabeth up to protect her.

quote: He's not the one who became Reddington. I did go into those banks. I impersonated your father for a few days, long enough to withdraw the $40 million. Long enough for me to realize how valuable a new Reddington could be.
context: Katarina reveals that she, not Ilya, originally impersonated Reddington.

quote: I made a promise the day you were born. To protect you. I realized I couldn't be part of your life, but that didn't mean I couldn't watch over you.
context: Katarina explains her decision to create Reddington as a protector.

quote: You see, the thing about buying a Soviet Nest is that it comes fully loaded with herring, vodka, and chlorine trifluoride, which of all the chemical gasses is, of course, the most flammable.
context: Reddington reveals the bunker's hidden defensive capability as he prepares to repel Townsend.

quote: I've waited years for this. I can wait a few minutes to break through some flimsy hatch in the floor.
context: Reddington is trapped in a bunker with Townsend, who is waiting to kill him; Red comments on Townsend's impatience.

quote: So I constructed him. Someone powerful and feared. Someone who traded in the very secrets that could help him monitor the danger around you.
context: Katarina describes how she built the Reddington persona to protect Elizabeth.

quote: The truth is, Masha, is that you were conceived as part of a lie. But it shouldn't surprise you.
context: Katarina begins her story, revealing the lie of Elizabeth's conception.

quote: My father was not only part of that system, he helped to build it. And because I was the son my father never had, he decided early on that I'd follow in those footsteps, which my mother disapproved of.
context: Katarina (as Katarina) tells Elizabeth about her childhood and her father's expectations.

quote: The source of my power is right here. She won't be destroyed. Certainly not by the likes of you.
context: Reddington declares that Elizabeth is the true source of his power, just before he sets off the gas.

quote: I'm dying. Whether it's this year or the next doesn't matter. What I've got doesn't go away. It just takes a pause, regroups, and comes back stronger, deadlier.
context: Red reveals the terminal nature of his illness to Lizzie, explaining it will inevitably return.

quote: Before I die I need to make sure you're protected... By showing the world that you're a force to be reckoned with, that you did what no one else could — no law-enforcement agency, no criminal rival — you found and executed Raymond Reddington.
context: Red proposes Lizzie kill him to secure her future as his heir and protect her from enemies.

quote: I don't know. I've thought and thought about it. And I just don't know. What I do know is that whether it's chance or karma, DNA or fate, or just bad luck — this is where you are now.
context: Red reflects on whether Lizzie's fate was predetermined or shaped by his influence.

quote: I'd give almost anything to hear you talk like a member of the Lollipop Guild.
context: Red jokes about Aram smoking marijuana during a tense moment.

quote: I've heard that one's true colors emerge at the end. I'd love to think that magnanimity is one of mine.
context: Cooper accuses Red of being magnanimous; Red reflects on his own nature as death approaches.

quote: I'm always prepared to die.
context: Dembe questions Red's willingness to die for Lizzie; Red gives a simple, profound answer.

quote: Only when I'm gone. Give it to Elizabeth, but only when I'm gone.
context: Red instructs Dembe to deliver a letter to Lizzie only after his death.

quote: Because if you knew beforehand, you'd never agree to kill me.
context: Red explains why Lizzie cannot know his true identity until after his death.

quote: This is who you've become. A criminal. A fugitive. And taking my life is a way forward.
context: Red explains to Lizzie that embracing her criminal identity through killing him is her path.

quote: Of all the times I've wanted to kill you, I don't think I can pull the trigger.
context: Lizzie expresses doubt about killing Red; he reassures her in a tender moment.

quote: Mother Nature and the criminal world quickly exploit a vacuum.
context: After Townsend's death, Red tells Lizzie they must act quickly to prevent chaos.

quote: Criminal empires are like authoritarian regimes. Most often ruled by a single, all-powerful leader. When that power becomes decentralized or fractured, it leads to a period of chaos and instability. So when the leader of a criminal organization steps down or dies, there's inevitably a rise in crime as others fight for control over what he left behind.
context: Reddington appears on a news program to discuss the rise in crime after his own absence, explaining the analogy to authoritarian regimes.
character_addressed: TV interviewer (and by extension, the public)

quote: Keeping the girl from him is cruel. Is that what you want? To be cruel?
context: Reddington confronts Cooper about keeping Agnes away from him, accusing him of cruelty.

quote: I recently spent time in a monastery above Boudhanath with sweeping views of Kathmandu, meditating alongside 36 Tibetan monks. I achieved an inner harmony there that was more mind-blowing than any psychedelic, and yet more fragile than an origami swan. That has to be cared for. If I stay here, it will be torn and crushed.
context: Reddington explains why he can't return to help with the Skinner case, describing his fragile inner peace.

quote: During the past two years, I've learned what to hold onto and what to let go of. If I look at that, if I come back, even once — I fear all that work will be for nothing. There would be names to be taken, people would be held accountable. Down the line, things would get very dark.
context: Reddington refuses to look at the tattoo of the Skinner's symbol, explaining his hard-won peace in hiding from the world.

quote: We all have dead skin. All of us. And healing will be slow and painful. But seeing you here, I can't think of a better way to start.
context: Reddington visits Dembe in the hospital and compares the painful medical debridement to their shared emotional healing.

quote: I'm not here just to help you, Harold. I'm here because it's what she would want.
context: Reddington explains why he's helping the task force, honoring Elizabeth Keen's memory.

quote: I'll let you in on a little secret, Harold. The world doesn't belong to the young. The world belongs to anyone with the strength to reach out and take it. And for the first time in a long while, I'm feeling stronger than ever.
context: Reddington imparts a philosophical secret about power and resilience, signaling his renewed vigor.

quote: I don't mind ruthless. In fact, I'm quite aroused by it. It's stupidity that dries me like the Sahara.
context: Reddington rebukes Anderson for his reckless actions, contrasting effective ruthlessness with foolishness.

quote: I once knew a man in Marrakech who... Actually, no. That was Tripoli. I was once struck by lightning on a golf course while playing in Tripoli. Gaddafi was dead, and to honor the small part I played in his unceremonious demise, the leader of the NTC invited me to play a round on the dictator's private course. One minute, I'm standing on the 12th green, the next, I'm in a desert encampment with a lovely raven-haired freedom fighter who's administering to my burns with the touch of a lover's stroke.
context: Reddington tells a parable about being struck by lightning to illustrate the unexpected consequences of interfering with The Skinner.

quote: I'm the president of my condo association. Garbage pick-up. Grounds management. That's what I do now, argue about yard signs with snowbirds, not try and talk sense to a lunatic.
context: Reddington mocks Vincent Duke's mundane retirement, contrasting it with the high-stakes situation.

quote: Why do you care about our reputation? Anderson is the 22nd Skinner, twenty-two generations of torch-passing. I couldn't do it once. I admire what you all have built.
context: Reddington explains his respect for the Skinner organization's legacy, despite his own failed attempt.

quote: I can tell you, one of life's great simple pleasures is seeing a woman, naked, out on the porch, with a bowl of hot water shaving her legs with a straight razor. It's captivating.
context: Reddington shares a vivid, sensual memory from his life with Weecha, contrasting his rustic lifestyle with the task force's urgency.

quote: It's good to be back, old friend.
context: Reddington acknowledges his return to the task force and their renewed partnership.

quote: I love surprises. Not all surprises, of course, but, you know, happy accidents. Finding forgotten money in a pocket. Making unexpected friendships.
context: Reddington reflects on the positive surprises life offers after their successful operation.

quote: I'm not an End Timer by nature, and my idea of rapture is, of late, a bit more solipsistic. But no matter what floats one's funereal boat, you will be judged by what you do in the next 60 seconds.
context: Reddington confronts the radical SPK members holding a church hostage, threatening them with judgment.

quote: Paychecks are the shackles of the common man. Remember that.
context: Reddington comments on Aram's return to work and mentions of a paycheck.

quote: As a matter of survival, I make it a point to only enter spaces whose borders I define. But if spending time with Agnes requires submitting to borders defined by you and Charlene, so be it. I don't like it, but the alternative is far worse.
context: Reddington agrees to supervised visitation with Agnes, acknowledging the compromise.

quote: You're my friend. This, what I'm doing here, I consider an act of friendship. You don't see it now. I hope someday that you will.
context: Reddington allows Dembe to arrest Vesco, framing it as a favor to his friend.

quote: It is. And mine is constantly being questioned. Because your feet are planted in two different worlds.
context: Dembe questions Reddington's loyalty after helping Vesco; Reddington reflects on his own divided nature.

quote: There won't always be good days. I know. And, uh, on those, I may regret my choice, but not much. And on the good days, I can't think of anywhere else I'd rather be.
context: Reddington comforts Aram after he chooses to stay in the FBI over his company.

quote: You're way past saving. I preserved you. An act of pure selfishness.
context: After saving Vesco from the SPK, Reddington dismisses any notion of altruism.

quote: There is an avenging angel for all of us.
context: Reddington says this to Michael just before she is shot, acknowledging that even she will meet her own reckoning.

quote: In the case of history repeating itself, I stole it. I realize it's no recompense, but maybe after all these years, it's sentimental reparation.
context: Reddington returns a Nazi-looted Van Gogh painting to its rightful owner's daughter, with a touch of rueful wit.
character_addressed: Ada (daughter of Van Gogh painting's owner)

quote: Order. Harmony. Balancing the scales. So good is rewarded and evil is punished. Most of us want that. I know I certainly do.
context: Reddington explains his worldview to Michael while trying to stop her from killing Huntley.

quote: In my experience, you can't have too many of those in your debt.
context: Reddington explains why he spared Huntley — not out of mercy, but to gain a powerful ally.

quote: What I meant was people will not think that I killed you. They will hear your confession and think that you killed yourself.
context: Reddington-style dark humor as he clarifies his threat to McHenry in the flashback — not a lie, just a technicality.

quote: In your binary world, that's all you see, so when you do your math, the answer you come to is that he deserves to die. My math is different.
context: Reddington challenges Michael's black-and-white justice, arguing for a more nuanced calculation of a person's worth.

quote: By every other day. We all have the devil in us, Harold, but the best of us have angels, too.
context: Reddington finishes his explanation of his moral standard — judging a person by the sum of their life, not the worst moment.

quote: You read that online prayer group? A bunch of it, yeah. What were they posting on there? Tragedy, grief, confession. Our blacklister waded through a lot of anguish to find her needles in the haystack. She takes advantage of people searching for peace.
context: Reddington analyzes how the Avenging Angel selects her targets by preying on vulnerable people in online prayer groups.

quote: What can I say? Apres moi le deluge.
context: Reddington, after returning the painting, shrugs off his actions with a classic French fatalistic phrase.

quote: We all have the devil in us, Harold. But the best of us have angels too.
She judged people based on their worst day, by the most terrible sin they committed. I don't think so. If that were the standard, we'd all be found wanting.
context: Reddington explains the difference between his code and the Avenging Angel's, arguing against judging solely by failures.

quote: True story: Calculus was discovered independently by Newton and Leibniz. A great leap forward imagined simultaneously. In my experience, great leaps forward usually are.
context: Reddington uses the story of calculus to suggest DARPA has a second team working on directed energy weapons.

quote: You're in when it suits you and you're out when it doesn't? Why does it have to be one way or the other? Why can't it just be?
context: Reddington confronts Dembe about his indecisive loyalty after Dembe refuses to kill Jovan for him.

quote: An eye for an eye. Jovan. He knows about us, or he's about to find out. I killed Sima to protect you. I want you to kill Jovan to protect me.
context: Reddington asks Dembe for a reciprocal act of loyalty in return for his protection.

quote: I don't draw a breath without knowing my perimeter is secure. It's why I'm still alive.
context: Reddington is confronted by a gunman in his home and calmly explains why he's still alive.

quote: Killing an agent who was a former associate is both stupid and bad business. They'd only assign even more than the usual number of buzzcuts to find me.
context: Reddington advises Jovan not to kill Dembe, an FBI agent and former associate.

quote: You can't sacrifice yourself for him. In the past, yes, but not today. He was in. Now he's out. This is the consequence, and you have to accept it.
context: Reddington tells Dembe he cannot sacrifice himself to help Dembe because Dembe is an FBI agent.

quote: So, to be clear, I'm not here to tell you to stop being angry or to judge you. No. My goal is to help you stop judging yourselves and each other.
context: Reddington mimics Dr. Sand's therapeutic approach to de-escalate a conflict among three mob enforcers.

quote: Listen, I'm a criminal, and however realized I may be is due in large part to shrinks and shamans, rabbis and monks. They hold me together like a psychological bandage, without which my sufferings would be insufferable.
context: Reddington explains why he believes a mob therapist is effective, comparing his own reliance on various mentors and healers.

quote: I found peace and tranquility and a real feeling of quiet. Yet, I abandoned it out of this compulsion for chaos and peril. I had found light. Yet I'm compelled by the dark. It animates me, so much so that I drag others into it. Others that I care desperately about. So, what is the purpose? If I'm willing to risk everything good in my life, to even defend risking it as necessary or just, when I know the result will only be a deepening darkness.
context: Reddington reflects on his inner turmoil and the recent betrayal by his oldest friend, questioning the purpose of his compulsion for chaos.

quote: Consider it a palate cleanser. A transition from a distasteful past to a delightfully piquant future.
context: Reddington offers Dr. Sand a three-month retreat on an island as a deal to work for him.

quote: So, the idea — well, at least the idea I came up with after spending my grandparents' entire inheritance on therapy — is to not hate yourself because you have dark impulses, but to love yourself in spite of them.
context: Reddington shares his personal philosophy about self-acceptance and dark impulses, ending with a humorous personal anecdote.

quote: Ah, first of all, we both know who you do it for, and it sure ain't me. And secondly, yeah, I'm threatening you. That's what I do.
context: Reddington confronts Dr. Sand after she claims to be the best at making people feel good, revealing his true purpose.

quote: The details of my story are not for the faint of heart. Based on your history, I believe you can stomach pretty much anything.
context: Reddington explains why he chose her as his personal therapist, acknowledging her dark past.

quote: Your job wasn't to tell my story the way you wanted it told. Whether or not you were at peace with my decision was irrelevant to what I hired you to do. You had a job. And for decades, you did it better than anyone possibly could. Until you didn't.
context: Reddington confronts someone about their betrayal in telling Elizabeth the letter's contents, connecting it to Vandyke's presence and her death.

quote: Sports predates math. History began with writing, and sports began 7,000 years before people learned to write. Sports isn't just as old as man. It is essential to mankind.
context: Reddington reflects on the ancient and essential nature of sports, setting up a critique of doping.

quote: When I was a child, my parents took me to Greece, to see the wonders of the world. I slept through the Parthenon, I was bored to tears at Thermopylae, but when I got to Olympia and saw the remains of the first Olympic stadium, I was overwhelmed.
context: Reddington shares a childhood memory about visiting Olympia, contrasting his boredom with other sites.

quote: If you look hard enough, you'll find there's more to every story. But that doesn't mean you should.
context: Reddington asks Mierce to give Vandyke's phone to Tadashi for GPS history, and Mierce warns him about dwelling on the past.

quote: In my experience, people will do almost anything to hide what they're ashamed of.
context: Reddington responds to Cooper's doubt about Maier killing an athlete to cover up doping, defending his theory.

quote: Elizabeth is dead for many reasons. But it looks as if one of those reasons is me.
context: Reddington reflects on the blame for Elizabeth's death after learning of the betrayal and Vandyke's photo.

quote: Perhaps this will give you a jolt. It seems I'm under attack.
context: Reddington reveals his organization is being hit by a strike team.

quote: I don't want you to get hurt, Dembe. I just want you out of my life.
context: Reddington coldly tells Dembe he wants nothing to do with him, despite caring.

quote: I see dried-out and dark. Bad blood and betrayal.
context: Reddington interprets the shaman's flower reading as predicting trouble.

quote: I'd like to think I had that much energy once. On the other hand, if I did, it's depressing to think about where it all went.
context: Reddington watches Agnes rush off to school, reflecting on lost youth.

quote: You might remind her there was a time when a Black man or woman wasn't allowed to wear a badge or carry a gun. But thanks to trailblazers like Bass Reeves, Big Sam Battle who paved the way for us, we have the privilege of serving our community and fellow man. In fact, scratch that. It's not a privilege, it's a responsibility.
context: Reddington advises Dembe on how to explain joining the FBI to his daughter Isabella.

quote: It may be an alpha predator, but they only travel in packs. And something tells me you're not dealing with sheep here.
context: Reddington taunts Baptiste after being called a wolf, implying backup is near.

quote: Yeah, that night, I couldn't sleep. I felt like if I stayed, I would implode, that I'd collapse into myself like a black hole and cease to exist. So I left. I walked away and... And kept walking. Until I found Weecha and Mierce. And they helped me. And I helped them. I'm sorry that I abandoned you.
context: Reddington apologizes for disappearing after Elizabeth's death and explains his mental state.

quote: In my experience, there are wolves on both sides.
context: Reddington cautions Dembe about corruption within the system as well as outside it.

quote: There are two kinds of people in the world, wolves and sheep. The wolves take. The sheep get taken. Unfortunately for you, I am a wolf.
context: Reddington confronts Baptiste while he holds Isabella captive.

quote: You know, Raymond, I am not surprised you didn't anticipate the raid. You have been distracted.
context: After a raid on Heddie's operation, Dembe notes Reddington is distracted by Elizabeth's death.

quote: I'd offer you an alcoholic beverage to celebrate, but I seem to recall you have a taste for Yerba mate. I didn't show you the ritual when you were last here, did I? It's one meant to be shared with friends.
context: Reddington celebrates Heddie's release with a personal, warm gesture—the mate ceremony.

quote: Pirated? Heddie was just selling seeds to farmers at a price. If my associate is guilty of anything, it's simply trying to ease the economic strain on the hardworking men and women who put the tofu in your turkey, the cotton in your shirt, the beans in your coffee. Everything it means to be human.
context: Reddington defends Heddie's seed piracy as an act of economic kindness.

quote: Heddie may be just another cog in the machine of my organization, but she's a fragile and unpredictable cog, and she won't last long behind bars.
context: Reddington explains why he must get Heddie out of custody—her fragility as a weak link.

quote: One of the FBI's most powerful tools, other than me, is the federal wiretap warrant.
context: Reddington introduces the threat of Arcane Wireless by acknowledging his own value first.

quote: Looking for the person responsible for Elizabeth's death is hardly a distraction.
context: Reddington defends his obsession with finding who killed Elizabeth.

quote: Even if there was someone, which I doubt, finding them will not bring Elizabeth back. It only delays you healing, or, apparently, house hunting.
context: Dembe presses Reddington that his quest for vengeance is a waste of time.

quote: I need you, Agent Park. That's why I put the Conglomerate on the Blacklist. I can't afford to lose you.
context: Reddington admits his manipulation, revealing his reliance on Park for his mission to find Liz's killer.

quote: You once told me that you weren't honest with me not because I wouldn't like what I saw, but because you wouldn't, that you couldn't expect me to love you until you learned to love yourself. How's that going?
context: Reddington echoes back Park's own words to prompt her self-reflection after a violent confrontation.

quote: Wetwork is such a delightfully bland euphemism for the act of spilling blood. Leave it to the Russians to coin a phrase so dripping with sangfroid.
context: Reddington dismisses Park's concern about the Conglomerate with a sardonic observation on language.

quote: Most people don't realize that anger is the purest expression of care we have. Rage comes from a lack of control. A fear you can't protect yourself or the people you care about.
context: Reddington observes Park's anger in her file, framing it as a sign of her caring nature.

quote: Forgive me, I guess I was under the false impression that we were all adults here. Thank God we're not.
context: Reddington responds to Cooper's anger over Park's actions, defusing tension with irony.

quote: Alina Park belongs in the Conglomerate. In eight months, she completed four jobs. Four jobs so extraordinary, she received the Distinguished Intelligence Cross... awarded by the Agency for 'extraordinary heroism involving the acceptance of existing dangers with conspicuous fortitude and exemplary courage.'
context: Reddington defends Park's skills and past, showing his respect for her abilities.

quote: Ineptitude bothers me. A lack of originality. Margarine. This and most everything else up to and including Agent Park's trigger finger? Deck chairs on the Titanic.
context: Reddington justifies knowing about Park's assassin past, comparing her actions to trivial distractions.

quote: Ineptitude bothers me. A lack of originality. Margarine. This and most everything else... Deck chairs on the Titanic.
I think I know how to find the person who killed her mother. Because to find them, we need to exhume Elizabeth's body.
context: Reddington reveals his drastic plan to Agnes, setting the stage for the season's arc.

quote: I love reading quarterly reports, examining financial disclosures, regulating the market. The part of my job I detest is enforcement. Lately, it seems like all I do.
context: Reddington muses on his role in the criminal underworld, echoing legitimate finance.

quote: When my father died, I kept a little painting of his. He always wished he'd been a real painter. But at least there was the one. He took terrible care of it, so it's faded and torn. But it reminded me of him, so I kept it in the bathroom. Every morning, he and I would have a little chat. Why do we do that, talk to the dead? They're gone. Why do we talk to them? But they're not gone. As long as we're here, they're here with us.
context: Reddington shares a personal story to comfort Cooper about talking to the deceased Elizabeth.

quote: I was born to a dark path. It's the only path I know. I've learned how to recognize light when I see it. To stop and stare. I reach for it. In the hope that it'll shed its light on me. And every once in a while, I'm able to bask in its warmth for a moment before moving on in the dark. That's my life. Don't make it yours.
context: Reddington warns Cooper not to follow his dark path after Cooper expresses despair.

quote: Oh, it's the classic love story. Boy meets girl, girl betrays boy, boy has psychopath dismember girl. It's so cliched, it's almost boring.
context: Reddington comments on a criminal's romantic betrayal leading to murder.

quote: Repayment in full, plus 20%. And fingers. Two from you. Two from you. Three from you. From the hand you used to sign your consent form.
context: Reddington pronounces punishment on cheaters at the night market.

quote: I have no idea what 'to wit' means. I just love the way that it sounds.
context: Reddington reads from a rulebook during a judgment at the night market.

quote: Much of my world exists right alongside yours. People and organizations in our two worlds have the same needs. Security. Medical care. Air travel. Corporate infrastructure. Financial services.
context: Reddington explains the parallel criminal underworld to Cooper.

quote: If they're gonna cheat, cheat the stock market, not the night market.
context: Reddington advises a cheating investor during the punishment scene.

quote: The first stock exchange started in Belgium, 1531, and for the next five centuries, this flow of capital transformed the world more than politics, religion, war.
context: Reddington explains the history of stock exchanges to a group of criminals at the night market.

quote: She's dead. She can't be disturbed because she doesn't exist. We exist. We hurt. We are in pain. And we need answers.
context: Reddington argues for exhuming Elizabeth's body to find the truth.

quote: Of all the ridiculous capers we've gotten into, this is approaching the most ridiculous.
context: Reddington and Cassandra pretend to search for a necklace they've already stolen from Matilda.

quote: My dear, you may have just written my epitaph.
context: Cassandra says she'll have to hate Reddington for double-crossing her, and he wryly responds.

quote: You've gone soft, Raymond. The old you would've meted out the delicious punishment that hateful old crone deserved on the spot. No regrets.
context: Cassandra comments on Reddington's decision to spare Matilda instead of taking revenge.

quote: This is a glimpse into the future I'm not sure I want to see.
context: Reddington observes the lifelike robots at Genuine Models and expresses unease.

quote: Everything went. Whether it went okay or not remains to be seen.
context: Reddington responds vaguely when asked about his 'matter' at Genuine Models, reflecting on the moral ambiguity of the situation.

quote: The man you once knew died the day Elizabeth Keen was shot. And the man that remains is less a person than a collection of impulses and inclinations, most of them foul as tar.
context: Reddington explains how Lizzie's death fundamentally changed him, rejecting Cassandra's nostalgia.

quote: I only survived thanks to the love and solace of a woman I met under the most unlikely of circumstances, a woman who carried me through an unbelievable darkness.
context: Reddington reveals his new relationship saved him emotionally after Lizzie's death.

quote: Assume the worst, hope for the best.
context: Reddington leaves Matilda the necklace and offers her advice as he and Cassandra depart.

quote: We're always good together. You know, that's why I've missed you, because we were good together, especially when we were bad together.
context: Cassandra reminisces about their past partnership, and Reddington agrees about their chemistry in crime.

quote: I hope so. But even if she won't, at this moment, I'm hers, and that's all that matters.
context: Reddington speaks of his uncertain future with Weecha, reaffirming his devotion regardless.

quote: I'm taking a reflective pause. I'm considering the extent of what I might do to get to the truth.
context: Reddington admits he is contemplating extreme measures to find Elizabeth's killer, reflecting the moral ambiguity of his quest.

quote: Cherish this time. The simplicity. Because it gets pretty complicated, I'm afraid.
context: Reddington consoles the overwhelmed new father Herbie by holding his baby and sharing fatherly advice.

quote: When nothing makes sense in the light, we have to search in the dark.
context: Reddington assures Senator Panabaker he understands her desperation after her daughter-in-law is found tortured.

quote: If you keep her happy, there is literally nothing I won't do for you.
context: Reddington, with a mixture of threat and charm, promises to help trace a medical device in exchange for keeping a woman pleased.

quote: Children have a way of surprising you. They're so resilient.
context: Reddington offers a rare, gentle observation to the Senator about the strength of children after a traumatic case.

quote: If you're willing to go this far, imagine how far someone like me is willing to go.
context: Reddington warns Panabaker that he is far more willing to cross lines than she is, showcasing his ruthless philosophy.

quote: I told you the day I agreed to come back that whoever killed Elizabeth would be held accountable. And I want that, too.
